Interpretable Quantities of a Structured Penalty

Source: R/structured_penalty.R
penalty_readable.StructuredPenalty.Rd

Returns the interpretable quantities that the structure declares through parameters7::param_readable(), in the shape that penalty_readable.DistribPenalty() returns, and NULL for a structure that declares none.

Arguments

pen

A StructuredPenalty() object.

theta

A named list of the structure's free values.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

NULL when the structure declares no quantities. Otherwise a list of four: value, a numeric vector of the quantities, each name the structure's own with the prefix precision_; jacobian, their derivatives, one row per quantity and one column per hyperparameter, with row names from value and column names from pen@params; transform, a character vector named like value that names the scale on which each interval is built; and block, the structure's label for every quantity, named like value.

Details

The hyperparameters of a structured penalty are the free values of its structure, such as the logarithm of a scale and the inverse hyperbolic tangent of a correlation for parameters7::ar1(). parameters7::param_readable() maps them to the quantities that the structure declares. Among the shipped structures, parameters7::ar1() and parameters7::compound_symmetry() declare a scale and a correlation, parameters7::scaled_matrix() its multiplier, and parameters7::autoregressive() the scale, the partial autocorrelations and the autoregressive coefficients. The other structures, among them parameters7::log_cholesky(), parameters7::inverse_of(), parameters7::ar1_inv() and the composition wrappers, declare nothing, and the method then returns NULL.

The quantities describe the matrix of the structure, and that matrix is the prior's precision. For structured_penalty(parameters7::ar1(4)) the scale is the diagonal entry of the precision and the correlation is the ratio of an entry next to the diagonal to the diagonal entry; they are not the variance and the correlation of the coefficients. For this reason the method prefixes every name that parameters7::param_readable() gives with precision_, so that scale and rho are reported as precision_scale and precision_rho. A structure placed on the covariance side through parameters7::inverse_of() declares nothing, so the method returns NULL for it.

Every link of the branch is the identity, so the hyperparameters are the free values themselves, and the Jacobian that parameters7::param_readable() computes in closed form is the Jacobian with respect to the hyperparameters. The method names its rows by the prefixed names and its columns by pen@params, and repeats the structure's label once per quantity to form block.

See also

penalty_readable() for the generic, parameters7::param_readable() for the quantities that a structure declares.

Examples

# An AR(1) precision on four coefficients: the scale and the correlation
# of the precision, named precision_scale and precision_rho.
pen <- structured_penalty(parameters7::ar1(4))
r <- penalty_readable(pen, list(log_scale = 0.2, z_rho = 0.5))
r$value
#> precision_scale   precision_rho 
#>       1.2214028       0.4621172 
r$jacobian
#>                 log_scale     z_rho
#> precision_scale  1.221403 0.0000000
#> precision_rho    0.000000 0.7864477

# The quantities describe the precision: its diagonal entry, and the ratio
# of an entry next to the diagonal to the diagonal entry.
Om <- penalty_matrix(pen, list(log_scale = 0.2, z_rho = 0.5))
c(Om[1, 1], Om[1, 2] / Om[1, 1])
#> [1] 1.2214028 0.4621172

# A log-Cholesky structure declares nothing.
lc <- structured_penalty(parameters7::log_cholesky(2))
penalty_readable(lc, list(log_L1 = 0, log_L2 = 0, L2.1 = 0.3))
#> NULL
